signal: Selerix acquired TBX (Feb 2025) and Steele Benefits (Sept 2025) to build an all-in-one benefits administration platform

email.body1:
Megan, saw Selerix acquired TBX and then Steele Benefits to build out an all-in-one benefits platform.

Two acquisitions in a year usually means a much larger addressable list than the team can personally cover before accounts cool off. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Selerix off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Megan, quick follow-up for Selerix.

After back-to-back acquisitions, the cross-sell and new-logo list expands faster than headcount can. Most teams never map how many meetings they actually need to book to hit the combined number, so the gap surfaces late.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Selerix needs to hit target this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Megan, last bit of proof for Selerix.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Selerix's reply rate likely compares to other benefits-tech vendors. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Megan, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Integrating two acquisitions is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a benefits-admin motion? I'll tailor it to Selerix either way.
